subtopics.title: The Job of the CRJ and Its Source Documents

questions.question: The Cash Receipts Journal records:
options: All money received by the business, in date order, for one month

questions.question: The day's cash sales are proven by which source document?
options: The cash register roll, totalled at the end of the day

questions.question: The Analysis of Receipts column answers which question?
options: What arrived, item by item, during the day?

subtopics.title: Recording Cash Sales — Two Truths per Sale

questions.question: Goods marked up 25% on cost sell for R1 500 cash. Cost of sales is:
options: R1 125 — take 25% off the selling price
R1 200 — divide the selling price by 1,25

questions.question: Why does the Cost of Sales column receive an entry when no cash moved for it at the till?
options: It records the stock leaving at cost, keeping the Trading Stock account truthful
It is a spare column for rounding errors
It should in fact be left empty

questions.question: One cash-sales line in the CRJ ultimately feeds which accounts at month end?
options: Bank, Sales, Cost of Sales and Trading Stock

questions.question: The forwards check of the mark-up arithmetic is:
options: R1 200 × 1,25 = R1 500 — cost times the mark-up factor returns the selling price

questions.question: The owner deposits R50 000 capital. In the CRJ this amount appears in:
options: Analysis, Bank, and Sundry accounts (detail: Capital)

questions.question: Why do Sales and Cost of Sales get dedicated columns while Capital does not?
options: Capital is not important enough to record
Frequency — daily items earn a column so a month posts as one total; rare items are handled by name in Sundries
Capital is recorded in the CPJ instead

questions.question: Which receipt does NOT belong in this term's CRJ?
options: Money received from debtors — that column only arrives with credit transactions

questions.question: The cross-cast of the CRJ requires that:
options: Sales total plus Sundries total equals the Bank column total
All columns add to the same figure

questions.question: Cost of Sales stands outside the cross-cast because:
options: It is always posted separately in January
It is not money received — it is the parallel record of stock leaving at cost
It is too small to matter

questions.question: Which practice does the analysis column directly support as internal control?
options: Exposing any gap between what was received and what reached the bank

questions.question: The diary picture explains the CRJ as:
options: A money-IN diary in date order, with proof attached, one page a month
A list of everything the business owns
A diary of money in and out together

questions.question: Sales earns its own column in the diary because:
options: It is a daily regular — a lane makes the month add up in seconds

questions.question: The tenant's rent payment is handled as:
options: A regular lane of its own, always
An entry in the Sales column
A named visitor — amount in Sundries with 'Rent income' written beside it
No entry, since it is not sales

subtopics.title: The Double Line — What the Customer Pays and What the Shelf Loses

questions.question: Sales of R1 500 at 25% mark-up on cost: what does the line show Thabo immediately?
options: R1 500 in, R1 200 off the shelf — R300 gross profit today

questions.question: The 'classic slip' when finding the shelf's number is:
options: Taking 25% off the selling price instead of reversing the mark-up by division

questions.question: The analysis column is pictured as:
options: The counting-tray — collecting each amount as it arrives until the tray is banked as one deposit

questions.question: The columns 'shake hands' when:
options: Sales total + Sundries total = Bank total
Every column shows the same figure
Cost of Sales equals gross profit
The diary has no blank lines

questions.question: The handshake fails by R300. The bookkeeper should:
options: Post the journal anyway and fix it later
Adjust the Bank total to match
Hunt the R300 inside the journal — usually a line with a number on one side and a blank on the other — before posting anything
Add R300 to Cost of Sales

questions.question: How does the CRJ protect the business's cash?
options: Daily intact banking, numbered receipts and the analysis column point at the exact day any rand goes missing
It replaces the need for a bank account
